Changelog

What shipped in every Rune release — latest is v2.35.0. Update with npm i -g @rune-kit/rune@latest, or run rune whats-new to see the newest highlights in your terminal.

v2.35.0Nov 28, 2026

"Proof" — Catch junk tests, read what's new after every upgrade, and zoom the skill mesh until the names are readable. rune serve is tested end-to-end through a real public tunnel (including a macOS DNS fix), with no VPS required.

ServeVerifyHooksPlatforms

Highlight

Junk-match pass

(rune verify --junk). Scans a test/production diff for checks that pass trivially or match on noise: tautological asserts (expect(true), expect(value).toBe(value)), catch-all regex (/^.*$/), empty snapshots, mocks that are only asserted to return what they were told, status-code-only behavior tests, and production code that imports test fixtures or snapshots. High findings BLOCK under strict hook-dispatch (preflight + sentinel); gentle warns. False-positive guards: expect(isValid(x)).toBe(true), specific regexes, mocks plus a real SUT assert, status tests that are actually about status, adding/renaming real asserts, and pre-existing junk on untouched lines.

New 6
  • rune verify --oracle <cmd|url|fixtures-dir> . Compares a candidate (--candidate <cmd|url>) against a reference oracle on a corpus: old binary, production URL, or recorded fixtures. Fingerprints each mismatch as {input, expected, actual, diffKind}, aggregates by fingerprint, writes .rune/oracle/run-<id>.jsonl, and exits 2 on *new* divergences. Known ones go in --baseline / .rune/oracle/baseline.json. JSON bodies are canonicalized; UUIDs and timestamps are redacted in fingerprint ids.
  • Reflect / generated lints (rune verify --reflect / --lints). Recurring review findings (.rune/review-findings.jsonl, count ≥ 2 or "promote": true) are deduped into .rune/lints/rules.json, a dated .rune/conventions.md entry, and a pointer block in AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md when those files exist. Nothing is committed — the command lists paths to stage. The same regex lints run in hook-dispatch. review, verification, review-intake, safeguard, and rescue point at the real CLI. Docs: docs/VERIFY.md.
  • Changelog page and "What's new" everywhere docs/changelog.html is generated from this file: version + date, area tags (Serve, Verify, Hooks…), one highlight per release, changes and fixes folded with counts, a filter by area, and Unreleased marked "on master — not on npm yet". The homepage hero and the Guide show a "New in vX" chip for the latest release; Changelog is in the nav of the homepage, Guide and Skills pages.
  • rune whats-new prints this release's highlights and the changelog link (--json for scripts). After an upgrade, the first interactive rune update / setup / status / doctor / … prints three highlights and the changelog link, once per version (last seen in ~/.rune/whats-new.json). Never on a non-TTY, with --json, in CI, or for hook-dispatch / serve / verify; RUNE_NO_WHATS_NEW=1 turns it off.
  • Guide: rune serve and rune verify sections A who-connects-to-what map, the 3 setup steps and what stays local for serve (a free core CLI); one card per verify check with the command, what it catches and the exit codes.
  • rune serve end-to-end test, no VPS needed npm run e2e:serve (scripts/e2e-serve.mjs) packs the CLI, installs the tarball into a temp prefix and drives rune serve setup --yes --json with the official MCP SDK client: handshake, list_skills / get_skill / get_reference / run_skill, 401 on no/wrong key, ?key= refused, path traversal refused, key rotate, stop / start, doctor, status, connect, and cleanup. --expose tunnel runs every check through the public trycloudflare.com URL; --service adds systemd --user (kill -9 → restart). The e2e — rune serve workflow runs it on Linux (local), Linux (systemd + tunnel), Windows and macOS on dispatch, release, weekly and serve changes.
Changed 4
  • One generator for derived site files node scripts/site-gen.mjs writes the changelog page, the What's-new chips, compiler/data/whats-new.json, the mesh diagram, the /skills/ badge and stats bar, and the Guide's layer table; --check (run by version-sync-check, so by npm run doctor and CI) fails when any of them is stale. npm run release runs it.
  • Release notes come from this file The GitHub release (publish workflow), the Telegram message and the ClawHub changelog use the CHANGELOG section (node scripts/site-gen.mjs notes <version> [--telegram|--plain]) instead of the commit list; a tag without a section still falls back to the commit list.
  • Mesh diagram is generated from skill-index.json It fits its frame at any size, shows the live counts, and highlights a skill's calls on hover, tap or keyboard focus.
  • Mesh diagram is zoomable and searchable Scroll, trackpad pinch, touch pinch, double-click/tap, on-screen +/−/Fit, or the keyboard (+, -, 0) to zoom and pan. Click or search a skill to keep it selected: its edges stay lit, a side panel (bottom sheet on a phone) lists the layer, a short description, clickable *calls* / *called by* chips and any signals, and labels are kept for the selection until you zoom in far enough to show every name. Layer toggles hide a ring; the diagram follows the site’s light/dark theme. The Guide iframe has an “Open the mesh fullscreen” link.
Fixed 5
  • npm run release failed after the site-gen check landed in #25: bump-version ran… npm run release failed after the site-gen check landed in #25: bump-version ran version-sync-check before regenerating the changelog page and what's-new files, so those artifacts were always stale. It now runs site-gen.mjs first.
  • rune serve setup --expose tunnel on macOS could report the new public URL as… rune serve setup --expose tunnel on macOS could report the new public URL as unreachable for minutes: its health check looked the hostname up before Cloudflare DNS had it, and macOS caches that miss. It now waits for the name via the resolver (waitForDns) first. setup --json also reports service.linger.
  • Mesh diagram: clicking a skill did nothing (only zoom worked) Mesh diagram: clicking a skill did nothing (only zoom worked). The stage captured the pointer on press, which retargeted pointerup to the stage, so the click never reached the node and was read as a click on empty canvas. The node is now read at press time and the pointer is no longer captured. Edges are also quiet by default (they were all drawn at once, a hairball): a skill's links light up on hover, and stay lit when it is selected. Covered by a real-mouse regression test on both the standalone page and the Guide iframe (scripts/__tests__/mesh-pointer.e2e.test.js; needs Chrome, skipped without it, required in CI).
  • Guide code blocks kept their line breaks only in the source: multi-line commands… Guide code blocks kept their line breaks only in the source: multi-line commands rendered as one wrapped line. They are white-space: pre again, copy buttons show on touch screens, and the Guide no longer scrolls sideways at 375px (platform tabs and tables scroll inside their own box).
  • Stale numbers: the mesh diagram said 64 skills / 203 connections / 40 signals (title… Stale numbers: the mesh diagram said 64 skills / 203 connections / 40 signals (title "57-Skill"), the Guide said "66 interconnected skills" and "13 AI coding platforms", /skills/ said v2.28.0 and 66 total skills. version-sync-check now also catches "NN interconnected skills", "NN AI coding platforms", the /skills/ total and badge, and the diagram counts.

Patch for rune serve found in a live Windows test (PowerShell, Node 24, non-TTY shell), plus a cheaper skill list and a release script.

ServeRelease

Highlight

npm run release -- <version> and npm run release:publish

(scripts/release.mjs). release bumps every synced manifest, renames the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] heading, updates the README "What's New" heading and runs npm run ci on a release/v<version> branch. release:publish checks the tree is clean and master equals origin/master, runs npm publish --dry-run and refuses on any npm warning, then publishes with --auth-type=web (2FA in the browser), waits for the registry, and creates the git tag and GitHub release from the CHANGELOG notes. --dry-run stops before the real publish.

Changed 1
  • list_skills is compact by default With no filter or tier it returns skill and pack names grouped by tier (about 1.2k tokens for 100 skills instead of 6.5k); detail: "full" brings back every description, and a filtered call still returns descriptions.
Fixed 5
  • rune serve <anything> --help / -h only prints the usage rune serve setup --help used to run the whole setup (start a server, handshake, print connect info). Help is now checked before any subcommand runs, for setup, start, stop, status, doctor, connect, install, key rotate|path, --stdio and --tunnel; a value flag no longer swallows a following -h.
  • The server key is never printed when stdout is not a terminal Agents, CI and logs capture non-TTY output, so rune serve setup, rune serve key rotate and rune serve install now write a new key to --key-out <file> or, by default, ~/.rune/serve.key (0600, next to serve.json) and print only the path. The --json report carries key.file instead of key.value there.
  • Non-interactive rune serve setup needs --yes Without a terminal and without --yes it now stops with exit code 2 and a message showing the --yes command, and changes nothing — it no longer starts a server on defaults by accident.
  • Windows connect hints use PowerShell On win32, rune serve connect and the setup report print $env:RUNE_KEY = "rune_sk_…" / setx RUNE_KEY … and "Bearer $env:RUNE_KEY" headers instead of export RUNE_KEY=… and $RUNE_KEY.
  • version-sync-check passes after a release Once a version is on npm, npm publish --dry-run refuses at the end with "cannot publish over the previously published version"; the check now still inspects the packed tarball for auto-corrections and the rune bin instead of failing CI on master.
v2.34.0Nov 26, 2026

"Serve" — install Rune once, use it from every agent on every machine.

ServeVerifyHooksPlatforms

Highlight

rune serve: Rune as an MCP server

Run it on a VPS (or any box) and connect Claude Code, Grok Build, Cursor, Codex, Gemini / Antigravity CLI, Grok Bot or your own bot over MCP Streamable HTTP — no local install. Four tools (list_skills, get_skill, get_reference, run_skill), a rune prompt plus one rune-<skill> prompt per user-invocable skill (slash commands in clients that show MCP prompts), and server instructions that tell agents the skills live there, so "use the video skill" or /rune video … just works. Serves Free core + packs and any Pro / Business tier the machine has (same detection as rune setup), plus --skills-dir folders. --stdio mode for local or SSH use.

New 9
  • Locked down by default Binds to 127.0.0.1; a rune_sk_… bearer key is generated on first run, printed once, and stored only as a SHA-256 hash in ~/.rune/serve.json (0600); rune serve key rotate takes effect without a restart. Per-IP rate limit, failed-auth limit, 1 MB request cap, 256 KB read cap, reads confined to the skill folder (no .., absolute paths or escaping symlinks), text files only, no shell execution.
  • Experimental: --runner claude|codex|grok run_skill(mode: "execute") runs the skill on the server through that CLI (argv only, no shell; prompt over stdin or a file), in its own ~/.rune/serve-runs/ folder, with a timeout, 1 MB output cap and concurrency limit, and returns the output and the files it wrote. User-invoked-only skills are never executed server-side.
  • Experimental: --tunnel and rune serve install --tunnel starts a Cloudflare quick tunnel through cloudflared and prints the https URL only once the edge connection is up (it says so when outbound tunnel traffic is blocked). rune serve install writes a systemd user unit with your serve flags (--print for a system unit), mints the key in your terminal rather than the journal, and prints the systemctl commands instead of running them.
  • rune serve setup: from nothing to connected in one command A wizard (or --yes --json for agents and scripts) that detects PC vs VPS, finds Pro/Business, creates the key (printed once, or written to a 0600 --key-out file so it stays out of agent transcripts), exposes the server (--expose tunnel downloads cloudflared into ~/.rune/bin with no root and opens a quick tunnel, falling back from QUIC to HTTP/2; domain prints a Caddyfile; tailscale runs Funnel; local), keeps it running (systemd user service with linger on Linux, otherwise a background process), checks /health, auth and a real MCP initialize + tools/list handshake, and prints copy-paste connect steps for Grok Bot, Claude Code, Grok Build, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Antigravity.
  • rune serve status | doctor | connect <client> | start | stop status shows pid, version, skill count and the local / public (tunnel) URL; doctor also probes both endpoints (set RUNE_KEY for the full handshake) and exits 1 on problems; connect reprints a client's steps with $RUNE_KEY in place of the key — the key is never printed after setup; start re-applies the saved setup after a reboot.
  • Agent runbook deploy gains references/rune-serve.md: the exact non-interactive SSH commands to set up rune serve on a user's VPS and connect their agents without the key entering the chat.
  • Docs and site docs/SERVE.md is now a 3-step quick start with architecture and setup-flow diagrams (advanced/manual setup moved below); the README and the landing page have a rune serve section with a diagram, the steps and per-client connect tabs.
  • New runtime dependency: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (+ zod), loaded only by rune serve New runtime dependency: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (+ zod), loaded only by rune serve.
  • Test-integrity gate rune verify --integrity [--staged|--base <ref>] [--json] inspects a test-file diff (Jest/Vitest/Mocha, pytest/unittest, Go, Rust, JUnit) and fingerprints assertion weakening: deleted or commented asserts, loosened matchers, added skip/xfail, snapshot updates, changed expected literals, deleted tests, assertion-count drops, and mocks that replace a previously real call. The same check is wired into hook-dispatch — preflight on Edit/Write of test files, sentinel on git commit. Under strict, assert-removed, skip-added, expected-changed, and edits to frozen paths (tests/char/**, tests/holdout/**, configurable in .rune/test-integrity.json) BLOCK, with a reason that tells the agent to fix the code, not the tests, or to get human approval. Under gentle, they warn. An auditable override (Test-Change-Approved: <reason> commit trailer or RUNE_TEST_CHANGE_APPROVED) is logged to .rune/metrics/gate-outcomes.jsonl as overridden. safeguard, test, preflight, fix, and verification now point at the real gate and the holdout convention.
Changed 5
  • Authoring tiers and adapter hints refreshed (2026-11-26) Authoring tiers and adapter hints refreshed (2026-11-26). fable is an optional frontier tier above opus (not a new default). Gemini CLI hints use stable-GA ids (gemini-3.1-pro-preview or gemini-2.5-pro / gemini-3.5-flash / gemini-3.1-flash-lite). Antigravity haiku hints Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Low) because 3.8 Flash leaves 2026-11-30. Codex gains a rune_frontier role (Astra at xhigh); Grok hints name grok-4.7 plus effort.   • Pro Context Intelligence hooks (platforms.<id> = "hook") install natively on Cursor,… Pro Context Intelligence hooks (platforms.<id> = "hook") install natively on Cursor, Grok Build, Antigravity and Gemini CLI instead of falling back to rules. Event mapping: Cursor beforeSubmitPrompt / preToolUse / preCompact / sessionStart; Antigravity PreInvocation / PreToolUse / SessionStart; Gemini BeforeAgent / BeforeTool / PreCompress / SessionStart / AfterModel.
  • statusLine-user manifest entries are not written into a repo file statusLine-user manifest entries are not written into a repo file. Install notes point at node "$RUNE_PRO_ROOT/hooks/rune-pulse/index.cjs" setup (Grok only reads a command status line from ~/.grok/config.toml; Antigravity and Cursor CLI likewise use user settings).
  • Manifest validation accepts the AfterModel event (matcher optional) so Pro hooks… Manifest validation accepts the AfterModel event (matcher optional) so Pro hooks v1.7.0 can load.
  • When Cursor hooks are installed, Grok Build skips the same Pro hook entries in… When Cursor hooks are installed, Grok Build skips the same Pro hook entries in .grok/hooks/rune.json so they fire once from the shared .cursor/hooks.json.
Fixed 1
  • npm publish on npm 11.21.1 was auto-correcting package.json and dropping the… npm publish on npm 11.21.1 was auto-correcting package.json and dropping the rune bin ("./compiler/bin/rune.js" is treated as an invalid script name). The bin path is now compiler/bin/rune.js (no ./), repository.url is git+https://github.com/rune-kit/rune.git, and compiler/bin/rune.js is marked executable. version-sync-check (and therefore npm run doctor / prepublishOnly) fails if a publish dry-run reports auto-corrected errors or a missing rune bin.
v2.33.0Nov 21, 2026

"Everywhere" — Rune installs natively in the agents people actually use in late 2026, and the numbers on the box are checked by CI.

VerifyHooksPlatformsSkills

Highlight

Install in one line, in your agent of choice

npx skills add rune-kit/rune (skills.sh, ~80 agents) · Claude Code /plugin marketplace add rune-kit/rune + /plugin install rune@rune-kit · Grok Build grok plugin install rune-kit/rune --trust · Gemini CLI gemini extensions install https://github.com/rune-kit/rune · Cursor plugin manifest · any Agent Plugins 1.0 client.

New 38
  • Three new compile targets — 16 in total rune init --platform grok (.grok/skills/), --platform cline (.cline/skills/) and --platform agents (.agents/skills/, the shared directory read by Kiro, Amp, Goose, Factory, Junie, Trae and others). rune init auto-detects .grok/ and .cline/ projects.
  • The Claude marketplace installs again Extension-pack ids were @rune/<pack>, which Claude Code rejects (14 validation errors); they are now rune-<pack>. claude plugin validate . passes.
  • rune doctor on every platform It crashed with EISDIR on all directory-per-skill outputs (Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, Copilot, Gemini, Qwen, Qoder) and flagged rune-pro / rune-business / rune-kit mentions as broken refs. Both fixed; a build → doctor round trip runs in CI for the new targets.
  • Every number is checked version-sync-check scans 26 public files (README, ROADMAP, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, llms.txt, manifests, landing + guides HTML, docs, the compiled branding footer) and fails CI on a stale skill / signal / connection / platform count. It found and fixed 39 stale claims (66 → 67 skills, 43/45 → 46 signals, 209 → 248 connections, 13 → 16 platforms).
  • Working buy links The README and the footer compiled into every skill linked to the private Pro/Business repos (404 for buyers); they now go to the pricing page.
  • A shorter README 73 KB → ~20 KB: pitch, per-agent install, platform support table, tiers. Every old "What's New" section (v2.6 – v2.32) moved verbatim to the bottom of this file.
  • AGENTS.md and llms.txt (also served at rune-kit.github.io/rune/llms.txt).
  • A Pro tip you can switch off The first red context warning of a session (120 tool calls) adds one line about Pro's real-% statusline. Once per session, never when a paid tier is wired, no network; RUNE_PRO_HINT=0 hides it.
  • Skills that other agents actually pick 23 skill descriptions (brainstorm, debug, fix, plan, review, test, sentinel, research, perf …) said what they do but not when to use them, which makes them harder for Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Grok to select on their own. Every description now says when to use it, and a test keeps it that way (natural wording counts, the literal "Use when" is not required).
  • Current model names Examples in skills and packs moved off retired or legacy ids (gpt-4, gpt-4o, claude-haiku-4-5, gemini-2.x) to the November 2026 lines. Authoring tiers are fable/opus/sonnet/haiku; adapters and hints were re-checked on 2026-11-26 (see Changed).
  • Cleaner output on non-Claude agents WebSearch, WebFetch and AskUserQuestion compile to neutral wording outside Claude Code, and onboard writes AGENTS.md (or GEMINI.md) instead of CLAUDE.md when it runs elsewhere.
  • No content lost on any platform Single-file targets (generic, openclaw, aider) silently dropped every skill's references/ folder, packs never shipped theirs (e.g. zalo/references/), and cross-skill reference links broke once compiled folders became rune-<skill>/. All three fixed: every reference file ships, and a test checks every link resolves on all 15 compiled platforms.
  • Leaner core skills — every SKILL.md now fits 500 lines Two passes split the 13 largest skills into a lean SKILL.md plus references/ files: cook (975 → 485 lines), ba, review, design, skill-forge, audit, session-bridge, test, team, context-engine, autopsy, brainstorm and plan. HARD-GATEs, frontmatter, mesh sections, Sharp Edges and Done When stay inline; a test proves every original line, connection (248) and gate survived, and the size guard is now 500 lines. Links between reference files resolve from the file itself, so they click through on GitHub too.
  • Look-alike skills now say where they stop Instead of merging, research / docs-seeker / trend-scout, problem-solver / sequential-thinking and hallucination-guard / completion-gate / constraint-check each name the sibling to use for the overlapping case (reasons in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → "Overlap Review").
  • Codex subagents on GPT-6.x .codex/agents roles: rune_heavy → gpt-6.2-astra (high), rune_standard → gpt-6.2-sol (medium), rune_fast → gpt-6-luna (high), per the Codex docs; verified offline with codex-cli 0.171.0. Antigravity skills no longer carry a model: field it doesn't support — a one-line model suggestion replaces it.
  • Worktrees outside Claude Code Compiled skills for Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Grok and the rest create worktrees in .rune/worktrees/ (Claude Code keeps .claude/worktrees/), and the worktree skill git-ignores the folder first.
  • Set up every agent in a repo at once /rune onboard --runtimes keeps one canonical AGENTS.md, points CLAUDE.md (@AGENTS.md) and Gemini CLI (context.fileName) at it, and proposes the right rune hooks install per runtime. New rune hooks install --platform grok writes native .grok/hooks/rune.json (Grok 1.0.92 grok inspect loads all five hooks).
  • Native hooks in Cursor and Gemini CLI rune hooks install --platform cursor now writes Cursor's own .cursor/hooks.json (preToolUse, postToolUse, stop), so completion-gate auto-fires in Cursor too. Your hooks in that file are kept, and the old preset .mdc rules are removed. New --platform gemini merges BeforeTool / AfterTool / AfterAgent hooks into .gemini/settings.json and leaves your other settings alone. Gemini's own gemini hooks migrate --from-claude produces the same event and tool mapping. Seven hook platforms now, up from six.
  • Rune hooks no longer stall edits in Cursor Cursor imports .claude/settings.json hooks and blocks a permission hook whose stdout isn't JSON; hook-dispatch printed a plain-text line there. Its advisory now goes to stderr, and --format cursor|gemini prints exactly the JSON each runtime parses. If the Cursor event can't be identified (no hook_event_name, cut-off stdin), it falls back to {"permission":"allow"} rather than {}, which would block a permission hook.
  • A fine-tuning example you can still run OpenAI is winding down self-serve fine-tuning (closed to new orgs; jobs end Jan 6, 2027; gpt-4o-mini isn't trainable), so the ai-ml example now defaults to open-weight LoRA with Hugging Face TRL + PEFT and keeps the OpenAI path for existing customers on gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14.
  • Hooks that actually gate rune hook-dispatch used to answer "allow" for every skill without running anything, so --preset strict could never block. It now runs the real pre-tool-guard (preflight), secrets-scan (sentinel) and quarantine scripts, plus built-in dependency-doctor and completion-gate advisories, and translates the verdict per runtime: Claude envelope + exit 2, Cursor {"permission":"deny"} + exit 2, Gemini {"decision":"deny"} + exit 2, Antigravity {"decision":"deny"}. Only preflight and sentinel can block, and only under strict; the rest are advisory. A crashed or slow (20 s) gate fails open.
  • Pinned hook commands Installed hooks call npx --yes @rune-kit/rune@<version> hook-dispatch … instead of an unpinned npx, so a hook never jumps to a new release on its own; rune doctor --hooks flags the drift after an upgrade.
  • Grok Build first-class .cursor/hooks.json entries are written in a hybrid shape (Cursor's flat command/matcher/timeout plus a Grok matcher-group hooks array), so Grok Build loads them with no "this Cursor hook won't run" errors; sentinel moved from beforeShellExecution to preToolUse + Shell because the two runtimes read that matcher differently. --platform cursor,grok (comma lists now work) writes one shared file and no .grok/hooks/rune.json, so Grok doesn't run every gate twice. .grok-plugin/marketplace.json uses a git-URL source, which grok plugin marketplace add rune-kit/rune && grok plugin install rune needs. A new CI job installs the grok CLI and checks the plugin and hooks with grok plugin validate / grok inspect.
  • Antigravity hooks rune hooks install --platform antigravity writes native .agents/hooks.json (PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop) and puts tier rules in .agents/rules/; the old .antigravity/rules/rune-*.md files are removed. Works for the Antigravity IDE and Antigravity CLI. Gemini CLI is noted as Google's enterprise CLI.
  • Model hints re-checked (Nov 26) Gemini CLI hints are stable-GA gemini-3.1-pro-preview (or gemini-2.5-pro) / gemini-3.5-flash / gemini-3.1-flash-lite — the previous 3.8 Flash / 3.5 Flash-Lite ids are experiment-gated latest aliases, not what a live gemini models run listed. Antigravity haiku now hints Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Low) because 3.8 Flash leaves 2026-11-30. Claude Fable 5.2 is a first-class fable authoring tier (optional, not a new default); Codex gains rune_frontier (Astra at xhigh); Grok hints name grok-4.7 plus effort. The oracle frontier class lists cross-provider equivalents.
  • Skills that trigger when they should cook no longer tells agents to run on "ANY code change" (it now leaves questions, reviews, one-liners and fully specified changes to fix), and skill-router no longer claims EVERY action. A new description-budget-check (in npm run doctor) keeps each description ≤ 500 chars, the total ≤ 20,000 and bans ALWAYS/NEVER/ANY-style shouting.
  • Paid packs fit every agent's skill budget Packs used to compile into one rune-ext-<pack>/SKILL.md with every skill body inlined — 55–649 KB, past Grok Build's 100 KB inline limit — and their references/ links pointed at files that never shipped (133 dead links across the Pro/Business packs). On directory platforms a pack is now a short index (SKILL.md with a "Skill files" table) plus skills/<name>.md per skill, with each skill's references/ folder copied and every link rewritten relative to the file that holds it (including links into core skills like plan/references/…). The largest compiled pack index is 42 KB; single-file targets (aider, generic, openclaw) still concatenate. <skill>-evals.md fixtures no longer ship as pack skills.
  • Claude Code buyers get their packs rune setup --tier pro,business copied only the tier's L1 skills (autopilot, council-cockpit, the Business orchestrators); the 13 paid packs never reached the Claude plugin. Setup now compiles each pack and installs it next to them as ext-pro-<pack> (index + skill files + references) — on Claude Code and on every directory platform. Re-runs refresh packs setup installed (marker file) and never touch a same-named folder it didn't create. Verified on a clean HOME with the real Pro and Business repos: 13 packs, 0 dead links.

v2.31.0Aug 1, 2026

"Measured, Not Grepped" — three checks that passed without measuring anything, and two motion rules that were confidently wrong.

Skills

Highlight

MOTION-CRAFT §10 is now role-first, and §14 covers SVG

§10 said "fewer and gentler, not zero", which is strategy-blind advice. It now asks the one question that decides everything — *is the motion sequence the content, or is it decorating a result that exists either way?* — then picks one of four strategies (bail / snap to end state / collapse transition / reduce complexity), each with a "under reduce it looks like" column, plus the hard rule separating snap from collapse. Live preference reads (change listener, never one-shot .matches at mount) are infrastructure on top of all four. New §14 SVG motion mechanics, previously absent entirely: user units vs screen pixels and why one keyframe set serves every size; the rule that rest must live in a base rule (which is what makes a flat animation: none reduce gate safe instead of a per-icon audit); pathLength="1", the 0.001 dash, 1.02 on closed paths; per-instance id rewriting; the six SVGO plugins that silently destroy an animated SVG at build time; viewBox framing and why getBBox() lies about optical size; clearance measured off ink rather than centrelines. §3 also gains velocity continuity across keyframe joins — ease both segments of a two-part move and the element dead-stops at the seam, invisible in source and obvious at 4×. §11 puts numbers on anticipation (~40–50ms), impact (~30% of the clock, origin at the base), and decay (0.6–0.7 per swing).

New 6
  • an outer if (reduced) return that runs before the helper applying the end state… an outer if (reduced) return that runs before the helper applying the end state — reduced users get the raw default DOM
  • one-shot matchMedia(...).matches with no change listener, stale the moment the… one-shot matchMedia(...).matches with no change listener, stale the moment the preference is toggled mid-session
  • duration: 0 on sequence-as-content, which applies every key pose in a single frame duration: 0 on sequence-as-content, which applies every key pose in a single frame
  • 0s while something awaits transitionend / onComplete — engines may drop the… 0s while something awaits transitionend / onComplete — engines may drop the completion event and the state machine hangs
  • JS timelines (GSAP / Motion / Lenis / canvas) left ungated, because a CSS media query… JS timelines (GSAP / Motion / Lenis / canvas) left ungated, because a CSS media query cannot stop them
  • a clean result is not evidence until the instrument is shown livecompletion-gate claim discipline gains rule 6: *a tool that measured nothing promotes nothing*. Rule 1 already said promotion happens by tool — but "no difference found" and "no measurement taken" produce the same output, and a silent instrument yields the cleanest possible pass. A null result may promote a claim to OBSERVED only once the instrument has been shown capable of returning something else. Three documented ways a check goes quietly dead: it examined an empty set, the target moved, or the harness itself is the bug. verification enforces the same at the protocol level — every clean result must carry the size of what it examined (tests collected, files matched, rules applied), because 0 failed out of 0 collected is not a pass. Three new Red Flags rows cover zero-collection test runs, empty-target scans, and no-diff probes never shown non-zero.
Changed 1
  • No new tests No new tests. MOTION-CRAFT.md and claim-discipline.md are reference documents that no test covers — verified by grep, and stated here rather than left implied. The four SKILL.md edits are covered by the existing structure validator. 1,653 tests, 0 fail.
Fixed 1
  • MOTION-CRAFT gave bad advice in two places"Never ease-in on UI" was over-general. It is correct on an arrival, where a slow start delays the moment the user is watching most closely. It is wrong on a departure: a thing that leaves does not leave at its slowest, and gravity accelerates. Both cases now carry curves (cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.9, 0.35) departing, (0.55, 0, 0.9, 0.45) falling), and review's escalation trigger no longer flags them. Also named the trap: smootherstep starts at zero velocity, which is ease-in wearing a different name. Easing was chosen by name, which says nothing about whether the motion strobes. For a large rotation or long translate what decides that is peak = maxSlope × travel / duration against a ~30°/frame aliasing ceiling. Measured max slopes now sit in §3: sine-ish (0.45,0,0.55,1) is 1.82, ease-out-expo (0.19,1,0.22,1) is 5.26. A 360° turn therefore needs ~1050ms on the expo curve and ~365ms on the sine-ish one — 2.9× apart, with nothing in the source revealing it. --ease-out-strong (slope ≈4.3) was being recommended as the punchy default and is a bad fit for exactly this case; that is now stated. A rotationally symmetric part aliases at a third of its own repeat pitch, not at 30°/frame.

Six skills declared context: fork and left background unstated: cook, team, launch, rescue (every L1 orchestrator) plus scout and docs-seeker. All now declare background: false. v2.28.0Jul 22, 2026

"Reasoner's Blind Spots" — completes the reasoning wave started in v2.27.0. Every addition here targets the same class of failure: a check that *feels* done because the model re-read its own work and agreed with itself. Advisory throughout — no new skills, no new HARD-GATEs except where a claim is asserted without the act behind it.

Highlight

Model failure-mode table

, run alongside the existing bias check. The old table catalogs how *humans and organisations* misjudge (sunk cost, groupthink, planning fallacy) and says nothing about how the analysing model misjudges. The new one names seven: pattern-match satisfaction, template hijack, fluent≠true, prior-as-fact, frame adoption, completion pressure, surface blindness — each with what it *feels* like, because they are invisible from the inside precisely by feeling like competence.

New 7
  • Three tells , promoted to the front: the answer arrived instantly with high confidence; the draft never used one of the problem's stated details; two or three attempts failed inside the same framing. Any tell means re-derive — never repeat a failed probe harder.
  • Report gains a 🤖 line: which model failure mode was active in *this* analysis and… Report gains a 🤖 line: which model failure mode was active in *this* analysis and what was done about it. "None apparent" is valid only with the tell that was checked.
  • Surface-constraint verification for deliverables carrying a mechanically checkable constraint on their own form — banned or required characters, exact counts, positional patterns, strict formats, a diff that must not touch a listed path. Rune had no coverage for this class at all.
  • Five steps: expand the constraint (and decide how to count) *before* drafting → draft… Five steps: expand the constraint (and decide how to count) *before* drafting → draft away from the deliverable → verify with the strongest granted tool → repair and re-scan the whole artifact → ship byte-for-byte, because any post-verification rewording invalidates the check.
  • New HARD-GATE: "the output satisfies the constraint" is verified only after the check… New HARD-GATE: "the output satisfies the constraint" is verified only after the check ran against the exact delivered text. Re-reading the output and judging that it complies is not verification — a re-read always passes; models read their own output as tokens, not characters.
  • Step 5.4 — a checklist item ticked from source is a prediction, not an observation, and the imagined render is always flattering. Overflow, wrapping, contrast failure, misalignment and collision have no textual signature. Table maps each visual claim to what actually settles it.
  • Visual items in the Pre-Delivery Checklist are now marked 👁 — tick them from a… Visual items in the Pre-Delivery Checklist are now marked 👁 — tick them from a render, or mark them ASSUMED. browser-pilot added as an outbound call: when a browser is granted it is the strongest check available and costs one call. Advisory, not a gate — an honest short checklist beats a complete one full of predictions labelled as observations.
Changed 1
  • The 👁 convention and the ASSUMED marker both lean on completion-gate →…The 👁 convention and the ASSUMED marker both lean on completion-gate → references/claim-discipline.md (v2.27.0). This wave is where that vocabulary starts paying off across skills rather than living in one gate.

"Calibrated Output" — Rune had exactly one opinion about response shape (caveman, optimising token count) and no rule for what a style is *not* allowed to compress. That gap had teeth: caveman's "hedging dies" list, auto-activated whenever context hits ORANGE/RED, deleted phrases like *"I'm assuming the migration ran"* — turning an unverified claim into one wearing observed grammar, at exactly the point in a session where the agent is most likely to be wrong. This wave adds the layer that resolves it, plus a second output mode that has somewhere to live now.

"Hook Output Contract" — the other half of the Codex wiring fix. v2.26.1 made the matchers fire; this makes the hooks actually succeed. Codex parses hook stdout as its HookUniversalOutputWire JSON and reports anything else as hook: <Event> Failed, discarding the output. Rune's hooks printed bare [Rune: ...] lines, so every hook that loaded on Codex ran, exited 0, and had its output thrown away — the failure was reported once per event, with no indication which hook or why.

Highlight

What it does

Post-implementation, re-reads spec/plan/contracts as the SOLE source of intent, scans the ACTUAL codebase (present state, not the diff), and classifies every intent key: implemented / missing / partial / contradicts / unrequested. Dead-interaction trace walks element → handler → service → route → entity; the first broken link is a partial gap keyed to the story's AC. APPEND-ONLY remediation: CV-<round>.<seq> tasks with intent keys; zero gaps = zero writes + convergence.clean. Refuses to run without a spec (NO_SPEC — "converge without a spec is vibes").

HooksPlatformsSkills

Headline

New installTierSkills function

in compiler/commands/setup.js. Called by runSetup after installHooks succeeds. For each requested tier, resolves the manifest via existing resolveTier, derives the tier root from manifest.source (must be absolute — explicit guard), and copies every subdirectory under <tierRoot>/skills/ into <runeRoot>/skills/. Idempotent: existing target directories are SKIPPED (protects Free skills from same-named-Pro-skill clobber AND protects user edits of previously-installed Pro skills from being stomped on re-run).

Changed 5
  • The fix lands tier skills into <runeRoot>/skills/ at rune setup --tier <tier> time The fix lands tier skills into <runeRoot>/skills/ at rune setup --tier <tier> time. If a user upgrades the Pro repo (new skill added at Pro/skills/<new>/SKILL.md) WITHOUT re-running rune setup, the new skill won't appear in the plugin cache. Re-run after pulling tier updates.
  • Existing skills are SKIPPED — no automatic upgrade Existing skills are SKIPPED — no automatic upgrade. Version-drift detection only WARNS via the skip message; user must manually delete the target skill directory and re-run setup to apply an upgraded Pro skill. This is intentional (protects user edits) but may surprise users expecting auto-upgrade. A --force-skills flag is deferred to a future release.
  • When runeRoot resolves to the Free source repo itself (e.g When runeRoot resolves to the Free source repo itself (e.g. node compiler/bin/rune.js setup run inline from D:/Project/Rune/Free/), Pro skills get copied INTO Free/skills/. The maintainer would notice on git status. Production npx @rune-kit/rune setup resolves runeRoot to the plugin cache, not the source — pollution only happens in dev-mode direct invocation.

All-platform suite at npm test 1444 total (1 pre-existing flaky perf test in detect-invariants.test.js, 5294ms > 5000ms threshold under load, passes 542ms in isolation — unrelated to this fix).

Fixed 3
  • Security hardening built into the copy loop : - Path-traversal guard rejects skill directory names containing /, \\, .., or . (covers entry.name adversarial cases not caught by assertSafeTierName in tiers.js, which only validates tier names). - Symlink rejection — entry.isSymbolicLink() short-circuits with rejected: symlink (would escape sandbox) BEFORE cp runs. POSIX cp would otherwise recreate symlinks at dst, letting the runtime follow them outside runeRoot/skills/ at read time. - cp({ recursive: true, dereference: true }) — belt-and-suspenders alongside the symlink-entry reject. Catches nested symlinks one level deep inside a legitimate skill dir. - Partial-copy cleanup — cp is wrapped in try/catch; on failure, rm(dst, { recursive: true, force: true }) removes the half-written directory so the next run isn't silently locked-out by existsSync(dst).
  • Version-drift detection : when target already exists, readSkillVersion parses metadata.version from both source and installed SKILL.md (minimal regex scoped under metadata: block — no YAML dependency, immune to multiline description false positives). Skip messages distinguish already present (v1.0.0) from stale: installed v1.0.0, source has v1.5.0 — delete target dir to upgrade.
  • formatSetupResult partitions skipped entries : benign skips (N already present) vs security rejections (M rejected) reported in separate counts. Each rejection surfaces a ⚠ <skill>: <reason> line so operators can audit a compromised tier repo.

Highlight

quarantine (L3, new) v0.1.0

— PostToolUse advisory on mcp__.*|WebFetch|Read of **/uploads/**. Emits [QUARANTINE-NOTICE: tool_name=… untrusted_surface=true source=…] into next-turn hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. Default trusted-MCP allowlist (linear, github, jira, atlassian, claude_ai_Google_Drive, neural-memory) skips advisory; operator extends at ~/.claude/quarantine.d/trusted-mcp-allowlist.txt (read fresh every call — no daemon restart). Per-session disable via QUARANTINE_DISABLE=1. Telemetry: 1 JSONL line per matched call to ~/.claude/telemetry.jsonl — privacy invariant logs only tool_name + decision + source + session_id (NEVER tool_input or tool_response body). Hard self-timeout 5000 ms; advisory mode never blocks tool dispatch (always exit 0). Two reference docs: trusted-mcp-allowlist.md (default trusted list + customization rules), quarantine-discipline.md (<UNTRUSTED> author-time pedagogy + layered defense pattern + honest framing of advisory-only nature).

New 6
  • Free/hooks/quarantine/index.cjs — Node hook implementation. Reads stdin event JSON, applies tool/path matcher logic (mcp__ namespace check, WebFetch always, Read only for **/uploads/** segment match), emits PostToolUse additionalContext, appends telemetry. No LLM spawn (independence-of-reviewer principle — hook scans data destined for the LLM, calling LLM from hook collapses audit chain).
  • 2 new mesh signals — quarantine.notice.emitted (quarantine → sentinel, integrity-check), external.content.received (runtime hook → quarantine, registered in EXTERNAL_TRIGGER_SIGNALS whitelist as the entry-point fired by Claude Code's PostToolUse, not by an in-mesh skill).

  • rune doctor --hooks — new CLI flag. Reads .claude/settings.json, compares Rune-managed Free-preset entries against canonical buildPreset(detectedPreset).hooks, reports missing canonical entries (preset wired more than installed) + drifted entries (installed command shape differs from canonical). Tier-emitted entries (${RUNE_PRO_ROOT} / ${RUNE_BUSINESS_ROOT}) filtered out — those are tier-managed and have separate check paths. Exit 0 always (reporter, not gate — operator decides what to do with findings). Use case: diagnostic before users file "skill is broken" issues; local drift is a common cause of unexplained hook behavior.

debug v1.2.0 — Step 0: Build Feedback Loop

— new references/feedback-loop-ladder.md with a 10-rank ladder (failing test → curl → CLI snapshot → headless browser → trace replay → throwaway harness → fuzz → bisection → differential → HITL script). Step 0 fires before hypothesis formation when repro is slow / non-deterministic / multi-component. Skip if existing repro is already one command, deterministic, < 5s. If loop construction takes > 10 min → triggers 3-Fix Escalation (architecture is the problem, not the bug). Codifies "the loop is the speed limit" — fast deterministic pass/fail signal turns debugging into mechanical bisection.

Highlight

adversary v0.2.0 — Mode: oracle

— triggered by agent.stuck from debug (3 disproved hypotheses) or fix (2+ failed attempts). Dispatches a stateless second-model pass with explicit "no prior context" framing to break confirmation-bias loops. Bundle format is regex-validated ([SYSTEM] / [USER] / ### File N), token-capped (100k bundle, 4k per file, 12 files max), citation-required reply contract. Secrets auto-redacted before dispatch. 2 new reference docs (oracle-mode, context-bundle-format), 3 new evals.

New 5
  • session-bridge v0.8.0 — Detach Mode — async escalation protocol. When oracle-mode dispatches an opus-class second-opinion call, session-bridge writes .rune/oracle-pending/<sessionId>.json (pending record schema with idempotency hash, 10min default timeout, status state machine: pending → complete | failed). Primary agent (cook Phase 4 / team Phase 3) reattaches via filesystem poll between adjacent tasks instead of blocking. Cleanup of orphaned records (>24h) on every session start. 1 new reference doc (detach-protocol).
  • context-engine v1.1.0 — Mode: preview — pre-flight cost gate. Caller (adversary/team/review/audit) emits context.preview BEFORE bundle build with file list + estimated token count. context-engine resolves caller-specific threshold and returns action (proceed | warn | block). Per-caller defaults: adversary 50k/100k, team 30k/80k, review 40k/100k, audit 60k/120k. Env override via RUNE_CONTEXT_THRESHOLDS_<CALLER>. 1 new reference doc (preview-gate).
